sanskrit: vyāvṛttau patho gāvau vyasyau yugyā uta | vidveṣaṇaṃ kilāsitha yathainau vy adidviṣaḥ ||
english: Two cows turned away from the path, unyoked — they have indeed become a pair of enemies; you have been made a thing of enmity so that these two might be set at strife with each other.

sanskrit: vi kilaināv adidviṣaḥ śaśvatībhyaḥ samābhyaḥ | atholmukam iva khādiram agnir vām astv antarā ||
english: These two have indeed been set hostile to each other for all the successive years to come; and further, like a firebrand amid khadira wood, may fire stand between you two.

sanskrit: siṃhas te astu cakṣuṣe vyāghraḥ pariṣvañjane | agnir vām astv antarā yathā vāṃ na sahāsati ||
english: May a lion be before your sight, a tiger at your embrace; may fire stand between you two so that you two shall not dwell together.

sanskrit: vy adyaud vy atatanad vy āsthat kapaṭv iva | yā oṣadhe prasarpasi vy agnir iva tau daha ||
english: It flashed apart, it spread apart, it stood apart like a door split open; O herb, as you creep forward, burn those two apart as fire does.

sanskrit: vi vāṃ yantu hṛdayāni vi cittāni manāṃsi ca | atho yat tanvoḥ saṃgataṃ tad vām astu vidūrakam ||
english: Let your hearts go apart, let your thoughts and minds go apart; and further, whatever union there has been of your two bodies — let that be far removed from you both.

sanskrit: asti vai vāṃ vidvikam ubhau śayane antarā | viṣvañcau pary ā vartethāṃ yathā vāṃ na sahāsati ||
english: There is indeed a thing of enmity between you two on the couch; may you two turn in opposite directions all around, so that you two shall not dwell together.

sanskrit: trayaḥ poṣās trivṛtaḥ śrayantām anaktu pūṣā payasā ghṛtena | annasya bhūmā puruṣasya bhūmā bhūmā paśūnāṃ ta iha śrayantām ||
english: May the threefold nourishments, triply woven, take hold; may Pūṣan anoint with milk and ghee; the fullness of food, the fullness of the man, the fullness of cattle — may those take hold here.

sanskrit: imam ādityā vasunā sam ukṣata- -imam agne vardhaya vāvṛdhānaḥ | asmin trivṛc chrayatāṃ poṣayiṣṇur imam indra saṃ sṛja vīryeṇa ||
english: O Ādityas, sprinkle this one richly with goods; O Agni, ever increasing, cause this one to grow; may the threefold, nourishing power take hold in him; O Indra, endow this one with vigor.

sanskrit: bhūmiṣ ṭvā pātu haritena viśvabhṛd agniḥ pipartv ayasā sajoṣāḥ | vīrudbhis te arjunaṃ saṃvidānaṃ varco dadhātu sumanasyamānam ||
english: May the all-sustaining Earth protect you with her green; may Agni, in concord, fill you with iron strength; may the white gold, finding accord with you through the herbs, bestow luster, making you well-minded.

sanskrit: tredhā jātaṃ janmanedaṃ hiraṇyam agner ekaṃ priyatamaṃ babhūva | somasyaikaṃ hiṃsitasya parāpatad apām ekaṃ vedhaso reta āhus tat te hiraṇyaṃ trivṛd astv āyuṣe ||
english: Born threefold at birth, this gold: one portion became the dearest of Agni; one flew forth from Soma when he was pressed; one they call the seed of the Creator among the waters — may that gold, threefold, be for your life.

sanskrit: tryāyuṣaṃ jamadagneḥ kaśyapasya tryāyuṣam | tredhāmṛtasya cakṣaṇaṃ trīṇy āyūṃṣi nas kṛdhi ||
english: The triple lifespan of Jamadagni, the triple lifespan of Kaśyapa — the threefold vision of the immortal: grant us the three lifespans.

sanskrit: trayaḥ suparṇās trivṛtā yad āyann ekākṣaram abhisaṃbhūya śakrāḥ | praty auhan mṛtyum amṛtena sākam antardadhānā bhuvanāni viśvā ||
english: When the three fair-winged ones, mighty, came together threefold, converging upon the single syllable, they thrust back Death with immortality, concealing within themselves all the worlds.

sanskrit: divas tvā pātu haritaṃ madhyāt tvā pātv arjunam | bhūmyā ayasmayaṃ pātu prāgād devapurā ayam ||
english: May the green gold of heaven protect you; from the mid-region may the white gold protect you; may the iron of the earth protect you — this one has gone forward to the city of the gods.

sanskrit: imās tisro devapurās tās tvā rakṣantu sarvataḥ | tās tvaṃ bibhrad āyuṣmān varcasvān uttaro dviṣato bhava ||
english: These three cities of the gods — may they protect you on all sides; bearing them, be long-lived, full of luster, superior over those who hate you.

sanskrit: puraṃ devānām amṛtaṃ hiraṇyaṃ ya ābedhe prathamo devo agre | tasmai namo daśa prācīḥ kṛṇomy anu manyatāṃ trivṛtā vadhena ||
english: The immortal gold, the city of the gods, which the first god pierced at the very beginning — to that one I offer ten salutations to the east; may he assent with the threefold weapon.

sanskrit: nava prāṇān navabhiḥ saṃ mimīte dīrghāyutvāya śataśāradāya | harite trīṇi rajate trīṇy ayasi trīṇi tapasāviṣṭitāni ||
english: He spans the nine breaths with nine, for long life, for the span of a hundred autumns — three in green gold, three in silver, three in iron, charged with heat and power.

sanskrit: ā te cṛtatv aryamā- -ā pūṣā bṛhaspatiḥ | aharjātasya yan nāma tena te 'ti cṛtāmasi ||
english: May Aryaman stir you, may Pūṣan and Bṛhaspati stir you; by the name that belongs to you, born of the day, by that name do we rouse you on.

sanskrit: ṛtubhiṣ ṭvārtavair ity ekā ||
english: "With the seasons, with what belongs to the seasons" — thus is the one verse.

sanskrit: yajñaṃ yantaṃ tapasā bṛhantam anv ā rohāmi manasā sayoniḥ | upahūtā agne jarasaḥ parastāt tṛtīye nāke sadhamādaṃ madema ||
english: I mount after the sacrifice going forth, great with fervent power, with my mind, being of the same womb; being summoned, O Agni, beyond old age, may we rejoice together in revelry upon the third heaven.

sanskrit: taṃ prajānan prati gṛhṇātu vidvān prajāpatiḥ prathamajā ṛtasya | asmābhir dattaṃ jarasaḥ parastād acchinnaṃ tantum anu saṃ carema ||
english: May wise Prajāpati, firstborn of cosmic order, recognizing it, receive that; may we, having given what is given by us, traverse beyond old age the unbroken thread of continuity.

sanskrit: śyenaḥ suparṇo divyo nṛcakṣāḥ sahasrapāc chatayonir vayodhāḥ | sa no ni yaṃsad vasu yat parābhṛtam asmākam astu pitṛṣu svadhāvat ||
english: The falcon, the fair-winged, the heavenly, who watches over men, thousand-footed, hundred-wombed, the bestower of vigorous life — may he place within our reach the wealth that has been carried away; may it be among our fathers in the manner of the ancestral oblation.

sanskrit: etaṃ sadhasthāḥ pari vo dadāmi yam āvahāc chevadhiṃ jātavedāḥ | anvāgantā yajamānaḥ svasti taṃ sma jānīta parame vyoman ||
english: O companions of the assembly, I hand over to you this one whom Jātavedas has brought as a treasure-trove; the sacrificer shall come after safely — know him on the highest firmament.

sanskrit: jānīta smainaṃ parame vyoman devāḥ sadhasthā vida lokam etam | iṣṭāpūrtam anu saṃ krāma vidvān yatra te dattaṃ bahudhā vibandhuṣu ||
english: Know him indeed on the highest firmament, O gods, O companions of the assembly, recognize this world; O knowing one, step along in the wake of the sacrificial and charitable acts, to where what has been given by you is distributed in many ways among kinsmen and those without kin.
